scenes.en: Myth vs fact every parent should know.
scenes.say: Many families call a squint lucky eyes. Here's what every parent should really know.

scenes.en: The two eyes don't point at the same spot. The brain gets two different pictures.
scenes.say: In a squint, the two eyes don't point at the same spot. The brain gets two different pictures, so it starts ignoring one eye.

scenes.en: Fact: The ignored eye can become a lazy eye, weak for life.
scenes.ta: உண்மை: ஒரு கண் சோம்பேறிக் கண் ஆகலாம்
scenes.say: Myth. It's lucky, so leave it. Fact. The ignored eye can become a lazy eye, and its vision can stay weak for life.

scenes.en: Fact: A true squint doesn't go away by itself.
scenes.say: Myth. Children grow out of it. Fact. A true squint does not go away on its own. Babies' eyes may wander only in the first few months.

scenes.en: Treatment works best when started early. Glasses, patching or surgery, as advised.
scenes.ta: சிறு வயதில் சிகிச்சை தொடங்கினால் சிறந்த பலன்
scenes.say: Did you know? Treatment works best when it starts early. Glasses, patching or surgery may be used, as the eye specialist advises.

scenes.en: An eye turning in or out, head tilting, closing one eye in sunlight.
scenes.ta: கண் உள்ளே அல்லது வெளியே திரும்புதல், தலை சாய்த்தல்
scenes.say: Watch for an eye turning in or out, a tilted head, or closing one eye in bright light. Check family photos too.

scenes.en: A squint or double vision appears suddenly, at any age.
scenes.ta: திடீர் ஒன்றரைக் கண், இரட்டைப் பார்வை – உடனே மருத்துவரிடம்
scenes.say: See an eye specialist urgently if a squint or double vision appears suddenly, at any age.

scenes.en: Book an eye test for your child.
scenes.say: Don't wait and watch. Book an eye test for your child.
